title: 'देवरात' खण्डकाव्यमा मिथकीय आद्यरूप [Mythical prototype in 'Devarat' Khandakavya]
nepali: मिथकीय काव्यको वस्तुमा आद्यरूप आएका हुन्छन् । यस्ता आद्यरूप सामूहिक अचेतनमा रहने परम्परागत विषयवस्तु हुन् र ती विषयवस्तुहरू कथात्मक ढाँचामा मिथकका माध्यमबाट व्यक्त भएका  हुन्छन् । पूर्वीय ग्रन्थमा रहेको अजीगर्तको पुत्र शुनःशेपलाई राजा हरिश्चन्द्रको यज्ञमा पशुका रूपमा बलि दिनका लागि तयार गरिएको, विश्वामित्रले शुनःशेपको रक्षा गरेको र शुनःशेप देवरात भएको कथालाई मूल आधार बनाइएको छ । काव्यको मिथकीय वस्तुको आद्यरूपीय ढाँचाअन्तर्गत बलिप्रथा, स्वर्ग र नरक, मानवता, दारिद्रय र शोषण, मन्त्र शक्ति, श्राप, द्रव्यमोह, संरक्षकत्व जस्ता आद्यरूपहरू आएका छन् । यिनै आद्यरूप भएको देवरात खण्डकाव्यका माध्यमबाट आदिम समयदेखि हुँदै आएका विषय तथा तत्कालीन समाज कतिसम्म नृशंस र विद्रूप रहेछ र हाम्रा सम्बन्धहरू कतिसम्म लज्जास्पद बनेका रहेछन् भन्ने कुरा देखाएको छ । पूर्वीय मिथकमा आधारित यस काव्यमा तत्कालीन समाज व्यवस्थाका खराबीलाई देखाउँदै समतामूलक, मानवता भएको समाजको स्थापना आवश्यक रहेको कुरा देखाइएको छ । यहाँ पूर्वीय मिथकमा आधारित देवरात खण्डकाव्यको वस्तुमा आएका आद्यरूपको खोजी गरी त्यसका माध्यमबाट अभिव्यक्त युगीन सन्दर्भको अध्ययन गर्ने काम गरिएको  छ ।
american_english: In the textual domain of mythological poetry, a prototype is seen to emerge. Such a prototype resides within the collective unconscious and constitutes traditional subject matter. In existing texts, the son of the olden era, Shunasepha, is prepared in the form of sacrifice in King Harishchandra's yajna. Vishwamitra protects the son Shunasepha and makes the son Shunasepha the original basis of the narrative. Within the mythical structure of the poetic work, elements such as the sacrifice tradition, heaven and hell, humanity, poverty and exploitation, mantra power, curse, material attachment, and protective custody have appeared as prototypes. These prototypes, which came into being as such, portray the subjects and the contemporary society up to every person being cruel and ugly in our relationships, and make the discussion of the establishment of a Samata, humane, and egalitarian society necessary. Here, the work done to find the prototypes that came into being based on Eastern myths through the medium of the Devarat Khandakavya is the work of studying the contemporary context through the medium of the subjects and subjects expressed through its medium.
british_english: Within the domain of mythological verse, a prototype is observed to come into being. Such a prototype forms part of the collective unconscious and constitutes traditional subject matter. In earlier texts, the son of the yesteryear, Shunasepha, is prepared as a sacrificial offering for King Harishchandra's yajna. Vishwamitra protects the son Shunasepha and makes the son Shunasepha the original basis of the narrative. Within the mythical architecture of the poetic work, motifs such as the sacrifice tradition, heaven and hell, humanity, poverty and exploitation, mantra power, curse, material possession, and protective custody appear as prototypes. These prototypes, which have thus come into being, portray the subjects and the contemporary society up to every person being harsh and ugly in our relations, and make the establishment of a society that is equitable, humane, and egalitarian necessary. Here, the work undertaken to identify the prototypes that have come into being based on Eastern myths through the medium of the Devarat Khandakavya is the work of studying the contemporary context through the medium of the subjects and subjects expressed through its medium.
